name: Osteonecrosis

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: No universally accepted formal criteria; diagnosis based on clinical and imaging findings

criteria.description: Presence of localized joint pain, often in the hip, exacerbated by weight-bearing
MRI showing characteristic bone marrow edema and subchondral signal changes
X-ray evidence of subchondral radiolucent crescent sign or sclerosis
Presence of known risk factors such as corticosteroid use, alcohol abuse, or trauma

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Clinical presentation consistent with osteonecrosis plus MRI findings characteristic of osteonecrosis
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Early diagnosis relies heavily on MRI; radiographs may be normal in early stages

pathognomonic.symptomName: Localized deep joint pain exacerbated by weight-bearing
searchTerms: deep joint pain worsened by walking
joint ache when standing or walking

pathognomonic.symptomName: Limited range of motion in affected joint

common.symptomName: Joint stiffness, especially after periods of inactivity
searchTerms: hard to move joint after inactivity

common.symptomName: Limping gait due to hip involvement
Tenderness on palpation over affected joint

occasional.symptomName: Referred pain to adjacent areas (e.g., knee pain from hip osteonecrosis)
searchTerms: referred pain from hip to knee
pain spreading from joint to adjacent area
loss of muscle bulk by joint
joint fluid buildup on and off
symptoms of secondary joint wear and tear

laboratory: Non-specific inflammatory markers may be mildly elevated
No specific laboratory test diagnostic for osteonecrosis
imaging: MRI: bone marrow edema, double-line sign, subchondral fracture
X-ray: crescent sign, sclerosis, bone collapse in late stages
CT scan: detailed assessment of bone architecture and collapse
genetic: Rare familial cases linked to mutations affecting blood supply to bone
other: Histopathology shows dead bone trabeculae with empty lacunae and surrounding marrow necrosis

distinguishingFeatures: MRI shows diffuse bone marrow edema without necrosis
No bone collapse or crescent sign
MRI shows fracture line without necrotic bone

redFlags: Sudden worsening of joint pain indicating possible bone collapse
Inability to bear weight on affected limb
Signs of secondary infection or septic arthritis
references: Moya-Angeler J, et al. Avascular necrosis of the femoral head: pathophysiology and current concepts of treatment. J Bone Joint Surg Am. 2015;97(12):1076-1089.
Assouline-Dayan Y, et al. Pathogenesis and natural history of osteonecrosis. Semin Arthritis Rheum. 2002;32(2):94-124.
